{{Short description|German mathematician (born 1961)}}
'''Christina Birkenhake''' (born 1961){{r|born}} is a German mathematician specializing in [[algebraic geometry]]. She is a lecturer at the [[University of Erlangen–Nuremberg]], in the research group on algebra and geometry.{{r|agfau}}

==Education and career==
After studying mathematics at the [[University of Münster]] beginning in 1982,{{r|cauchy}}
Birkenhake earned her doctorate ([[dr. rer. nat.]]) in 1989 from the University of Erlangen–Nuremberg. Her dissertation was ''Heisenberg-Gruppen ampler Geradenbündel auf abelschen Varietäten'' [''[[Heisenberg group]]s of [[ample line bundle]]s on [[abelian variety|abelian varieties]]''], and her [[doctoral advisor]] was Herbert Lange.{{r|mg}}

She worked as a research assistant at the University Erlangen-Nürnberg, earning her [[habilitation]] there in 1994, until in 2001 she was given a chair in [[complex analysis]] at [[Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz]]. She returned to Erlangen–Nuremberg as a lecturer in 2003.{{r|cauchy}}
